t.1.58.1: When the king, who had visibly assumed the form of a caṇḍāla, had spoken these words, the son of Kuśika, out of compassion, addressed him in sweet words.
t.1.58.2: Welcome, O Ikṣvāku, my child! I know you to be most righteous. I shall be your refuge; do not be afraid, O bull among kings.
t.1.58.3: I shall invite all the great sages of meritorious deeds, who will lend their help to the sacrifice, O king; then you will perform the sacrifice free from care.
t.1.58.4: This form which now abides in you, wrought by the curse of your preceptor, together with this very form you shall go, in your own body.
t.1.58.6: Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant one directed his supremely righteous and greatly wise sons to gather the materials for the sacrifice.
t.1.58.5: I deem heaven already within your grasp, O lord of men, since you, having approached Kauśika, have gone for refuge to one who grants refuge.
t.1.58.7: Having summoned all his disciples, he spoke these words.
t.1.58.8: My sons, by my command bring here all the foremost sages, together with their disciples, their friends and their officiating priests, all of them deeply learned.
t.1.58.9: Whatever words anyone else may speak when urged on by the force of my command, all that was said, even if spoken with disrespect, must be reported to me in full.
t.1.58.10: Having heard those words of his, they went off in all directions at his command; then from every land the expounders of the Veda came.
t.1.58.11: Those disciples approached the sage of blazing splendor, and all of them reported to him the words of all the expounders of Brahman.
t.1.58.12: Having heard your word, all the twice-born are assembling; from all the lands they came, except for Mahodaya.
t.1.58.14: How can the gods and seers partake of the oblation in the assembly of one whose sacrificial priest is a kṣatriya, and who is, above all, a caṇḍāla?
t.1.58.13: Hear, O bull among sages, about that whole hundred of Vasiṣṭha's sons, and all the words they spoke, their syllables faltering with rage.
t.1.58.15: Or how will the great-souled brāhmaṇas, having eaten the food of a caṇḍāla, go to heaven, even though protected by Viśvāmitra?
t.1.58.16: O tiger among sages, all those sons of Vasiṣṭha, together with Mahodaya, their eyes red with anger, spoke these harsh words.
t.1.58.17: Having heard those words of all of them, the bull among sages, his eyes reddened with fury, wrathfully spoke these words.
t.1.58.18: Since they defile me, who am undefiled and have undertaken fierce austerity, those evil-minded ones will be reduced to ashes; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.58.20: Pitiless, deformed and hideous, living on a fixed diet of dog's flesh and known by the name of Muṣṭikas, let them roam about these worlds.
t.1.58.19: Today, led by the noose of Time to the abode of Vaivasvata, may they all, for seven hundred births, become eaters of the dead.
t.1.58.21: And the evil-minded Mahodaya, who defiled me though I was undeserving of reproach, shall himself be disgraced in all the worlds and shall fall to the state of a Niṣāda.
t.1.58.22: Devoted to the taking of life and fallen into pitilessness, he will lead a wretched existence for a long time because of my wrath.
t.1.58.23: Having spoken these words, Viśvāmitra, the great ascetic of mighty splendor, the great sage, fell silent in the midst of the seers.
